title: Perf run 20261016-2036
heading: No headline row moved; the bench now serves both sides as players are served
meta:
This run's one speed change, a year-long cache for a returning phone, is out of the PR. It made the start page usable sooner but the first click slower, on the same visit. That is a trade between two moments a player waits on, so it is saved as a patch and asked below.

What stays: a fix for a computer that could still search after its game closed, fixes that make the bench serve both sides of a comparison as the host serves players, and rules that now fail a build or a test when broken.

The target was every headline row 1.2× faster than the base 38d62be. It was missed: ×1.002 on af6886b (4 pairs) and ×0.987 on the head a571839, the same app code (8 pairs). The 4-pair run called reopening a long game worse; the 8-pair rerun of the same profile does not.

needs.intro: Four items. The PR does not wait on 2, 3 or 4.

items.title: Five headline rows lean slower on the final code; none is called
items.body:
The speed rule sends here every headline row that is slower in every pair or more than 3% slower at its median pair.

On af6886b against 38d62be, 4 pairs (ab-20261016-2036-final-af6886b.md):

  • reopening a long game, 190 → 273 ms, called worse, every pair slower: 1.40 1.35 2.13 1.35;
  • desktop start page usable, ×1.118 at the median pair: 1.14 0.77 1.10 1.14;
  • desktop first click, ×1.071: 1.31 0.95 0.90 1.19;
  • a picked-up piece, ×1.049: 1.11 0.94 1.05 1.05.

The same profile rerun on the head a571839 (the same app code), 8 pairs (ab-20261016-2036-final-a571839.md), calls nothing. Reopening is 240 → 237 ms, ×1.165, pairs 0.78 0.78 1.71 1.06 1.27 0.69 1.85 1.42, so the call does not hold. The other three are ×1.03, ×0.785 and ×0.985 there. Over the rule on a571839 instead, each slower in 5 of 8 pairs:

  • phone board on screen ×1.193: 0.97 0.93 1.32 1.32 1.21 1.18 1.27 0.82;
  • desktop board on screen ×1.105: 1.33 0.71 0.94 1.42 1.16 1.04 1.32 0.60;
  • the computer's first board picture ×1.073: 1.17 1.08 0.98 1.06 1.41 1.09 0.91 1.00;
  • the player's move ×1.073: 0.96 1.06 0.99 1.11 0.99 1.09 1.12 1.21;
  • reopening ×1.165 (above).

None of the run's own changes runs in these moments. The rows that lean change from one run to the next on identical app code.

items.title: The target was missed: about ×1.0 against 1.2× on every headline row
items.body:
Since main's b3d7a23, the skill asks every headline row to be 1.2× faster than this run's base 38d62be, at its median pair. The run got ×1.002 on af6886b and ×0.987 on a571839 (charts above: the dashed line is the target). The only row past it is the desktop first click on a571839 (×0.785, 13.1 → 10.9 ms). That row has two modes (ledger 1009-1606:Q1) and runs no code this run changed, so it is not a gain.

Why it was missed:

  • The run's one speed change is a trade between two moments, so it is out of the PR (the next item).
  • Most of the run went to making the bench measure truthfully, and to fixes and checks.
  • This target arrived with b3d7a23, merged at 02:40, after the run had stopped making changes. Until then it worked to the earlier target, 1.2× against the first recorded run, which stands at 2.48×.

No open ledger idea reaches every row: the cache patch and RB1 touch the returning phone, SP5 the desktop board, Q1 the first click.
items.recommend: Keep the target. Start the next run by relaunching the lenses for new techniques, hot paths and the main thread against the GPU (1, 2 and 5), asking for ideas that move every moment, such as the shared scene chunk and the first frame, before the ledger's single-row items. Or name the rows you want the 1.2× on.

items.title: Bring back the year-long cache for a returning phone? Usable sooner, first click slower
items.body:
Commit 98699f5 told the host to let browsers keep the built files under /assets/ for a year, and made a click on the start page take down a preview that had loaded but not shown. Commit 312cf84 reverts it. It is saved as bench/loop/patches/assets-cache-click-RC1.patch, which applies to the head, and ledger row 0930:17.

On f5615af against 38d62be, cold load, 8 pairs (ab-20261016-2036-final.md), a returning phone (4× slower CPU, Fast 4G):

  • was usable after 409 ms instead of 553 ms (−27%, called better);
  • answered its first click after 57.7 ms instead of 40.7 ms (+39%, called worse);
  • showed its board after 636 ms instead of 567 ms (+9.6%, not called).

Two checks come first, as correctness: a missing file must not be cached for a year as the app's HTML (AH1), and a test must cover a click that comes before the preview's code (ST1).

items.recommend: Yes, after AH1 and ST1. The page is ready 144 ms sooner, and the click, 17 ms slower, still answers in under 60 ms. The next run would land the two checks, apply the patch, and try RB1 on top (ask for the 3D code only after the page is ready) to win back the click and the board. Say no to keep it parked.

items.title: After a click in the move list, should the next Tab first show the ring? (1016:FT1)
items.body: When a player has clicked a move in the list and a new move lands, focus follows to the new move. Main does this with a plain .focus(), so the next Tab moves on. The parked form, bench/loop/patches/move-list-quiet-focus-FT1.patch, goes through focusFromCode like every other focus the page moves, so the next Tab only shows the ring and a second Tab moves on. This is a behaviour a player sees, so it is your call. It has waited since run 20261016-0037.

items.recommend: Keep main's behaviour, as the PR does. The extra Tab costs a keyboard player a keystroke, and after a click no ring is the browser's own choice too. Say so if you want the patch applied.

scoreboard.intro:
The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. This run's target: every one 1.2× faster than the base 38d62be.

On the head a571839 (app code identical to af6886b), 8 pairs (ab-20261016-2036-final-a571839.md): ×0.987 over the 15 rows, none called better or worse. On af6886b, 4 pairs: ×1.002, one called worse (reopening a long game), which the 8-pair run does not repeat. Three narrower runs against the base did not repeat it either (reopening alone −18%; after the start page, setup and computer −3.0%; in the full run's order +6.2%), and against main this run's code is −7.7% there.

Memory on a571839: geometries grown over 16 moves 10 → 10; textures 0 → 0.5 at the medians, +1 in the last four pairs only (0 → 0 on af6886b, the same code), over the 5% flag but not called; JavaScript memory after reopening a 2,000-ply game +0.2%. None of the 105 other measurements was called.

At the start of the run, 38d62be against the last run's base f294faf was ×1.050, none called (ab-20261016-2036-regress.md). For the long view, the last measurement against the first recorded run (92ce041) stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast over the 11 rows both can measure.

changed.intro: No change in the PR is for speed. Each one fixes behaviour, makes the bench serve pages as the host does, or turns a rule into a check. Each was shown against the base's code or a deliberately broken copy: the fix's new test fails on the base's computer.ts; the old bench served a game's address the start page and a base without the header code no security headers (curl); the old verdict calls a count that should never be called; the old scoreboard tool accepted a head with uncommitted changes, which the new one refuses; the night-colour test fails when either side changes. The run record's "Commits and evidence" has each result.

items.title: A disposed computer no longer runs a queued search (f5b2c71)
items.body: When the computer's worker fails to load, its searches run on the page, one after another. A search that was waiting in that queue when the game closed still ran. It now checks that it is still wanted after its short wait. New tests measure the gap between searches, check that a dropped search never runs, and check that a failing search fails only its own question. This path only runs when the worker fails, so no headline row can see it.

items.title: Both sides of a comparison are served as the host serves players (10b16c7, 64c3fa2, 190a4b5, 1fc6c71, f03c208, ca49f7c)
items.body:
• The bench's preview server now reads each side's own public/_headers, so the base side is no longer given the head's cache rule (10b16c7). The code that did this left the shipped vite.config.ts (−51 lines).
  • A game's address is served the invitation's page, as public/_redirects has the host do (64c3fa2). The shared-game rows now measure the page players get, so they cannot be compared with runs before this commit.
  • Two counts on the start page are judged in their own direction (190a4b5). Since #162 every comparison had called the early picture's count worse, by design.
  • Each run waits for the CPU to go quiet before it starts (1fc6c71). Runs now begin with under 2% of the CPU waiting, about 18 s after the last one.
  • The report's legend now says which counts are judged higher and which are never called (f03c208).
  • A scoreboard row measured on uncommitted code must now name the commit or the saved patch it measured (ca49f7c). This run's rows that said '+wip' now name their patch.

items.title: Rules that are now checks (3103ccc, a8c3660, aae20d5, 823d0b3, e322e61, 53ab6bf)
items.body:
• The build fails when the start page's code and styles grow past 121,000 bytes gzipped (116,562 today). It also fails when it cannot find the start page's CSS, so the sum cannot quietly shrink.
  • The page's night colour is written once, as --night, and a test ties it to the sky's colour in the 3D scene. The dev page that renders the start page's pictures reads it from the same place.
  • The e2e check that no move in the record is cut off now fails when it finds no move to measure.
  • The computer's tests reset their shared search log before each test.

removed.intro:
The bench's header code left the shipped vite.config.ts (−51 lines, moved into client/bench/preview.config.ts), and the lint rule for __r3fState states its message once (−10 lines).

Against main, outside bench/loop/: the app and its build config shrink by 22 lines net (+57, −79). Tests grow by 47 lines, the bench by 269 (the preview config, its tests and the verdict test), and ARCHITECTURE.md by 2.

rejected.intro: Each of these has its result in the ledger.

items.title: The click taking down any preview still loading, even before its code arrives
items.body: On a first visit, the phone's first click went 39.2 → 48.4 ms (+23%, every pair slower, not called): the click re-rendered the page where nothing was queued yet (ab-20261016-2036-cache-rc1.md, 6 pairs; patches/assets-cache-click-unconditional-RC1a.patch). The form that waits for the code was +0.5% there (-cache-rc1b.md); it is in the parked patch. Ledger row 1016-1616:RC1a.

items.title: Rejected on reading, without a measurement
items.body:
• A script-src Content Security Policy: the app has no place where untrusted text becomes code, and the policy would need hashes generated at build time that e2e cannot see.
  • Counting cache hits on the returning visit: the request count already shows it (14.5 → 2).
  • Escape closing the move list behind a dialog: everything behind a dialog is already inert.
  • The first form of the e2e record check: it failed at 360×640, 390×844 and 700×900, where the narrow list is folded away.

choices.intro:
• I reverted 98699f5, the run's only speed change, at the grade. The loop keeps a trade between two player moments out of the PR. To overrule, apply patches/assets-cache-click-RC1.patch.
  • I did not hold the PR for the 4-pair call on reopening a long game: the same profile rerun with 8 pairs does not call it, 14 narrower pairs did not repeat it, and this run's code is faster than main there. The rows that lean are under Needs from me.
  • I fixed the review's one blocker and five small items it raised. The other 11 items went to the ledger.
  • I merged main twice: #163 and #164 before the first checks, and #165 (the skill) before the final ones. The run followed the skill as it was at its base; this report measures against the merged skill's target (1.2× faster than 38d62be).
  • The exploratory bisect reports from the start of the run stay in bench/out/, which git ignores. No decision rests on them.

notConfirmed.intro:
• Why reopening a long game leans slower only in the full run: called on af6886b (4 pairs), ×1.165 and not called on a571839 (8 pairs) (ledger 1016:RG3).
  • Whether the start page's board leans against itself on a cold load: no 8-pair A/A since the CPU wait was added (ledger 1016:AA1). The desktop board was −11% on af6886b and ×1.105 on a571839, on the same code.
  • Textures grown over 16 moves, 0 → 0.5 on a571839 (+1 in pairs 5–8 only, 0 on af6886b): not traced. Nothing in the run's diff makes a texture.
  • The cache rule on a real Cloudflare Pages deploy (AH1). It matters again only if the patch comes back.
